dea-avc-001.text: Five applications consume the same Kinesis Data Stream in shared mode and compete for 2 MB/s reading by shard, elevating the delivery latency. The requirement is throughput reading DEDICADO per consumer and latency ~70 ms, without increasing shards. Which resource answers?
options: Reduce batch size
Enhanced Fan-Out: every registered consumer receives 2 MB/s dedicated by shard with push delivery via HTTP/2
Long polling in consumers
Increase stream retention
dea-avc-001.explanation: A) Incorrect: minor batch increases overhead and does not create dedicated throughput. B) Correct: the EFO creates a dedicated way of 2 MB/s per shard for CADA registered consumer, with push on ~70 ms — eliminates competition without reharding. SQS. D) Incorrect: retention affects replay, no reading flow.

dea-avc-002.text: A stream provided has 10 Shards, but A Shard receives 80% The current key score is the store code, and the matrix store dominates the events. DUAS actions correct hot shard? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Increase retention to 7 days
Reduce the total number of shards
Apply random jumping/suffix to the key of the dominant store, spreading your events between shards
Change the partition key to one of the following: ALTA cardinality and uniform distribution (e.g. event/client ID))
Migratory to SQS FIFO
dea-avc-002.explanation: A) Incorrect: retention does not change the writing distribution. B) Incorrect: less shards concentrate AINDA plus traffic. C) Correct: when business key needs to be maintained, the jumping (shop#1..N) divides the traffic of the hot key, reaggregating it into consumption. D) Correct: High cardinality key distributes the hash evenly between shards — structural correction. E) Incorrect: exchange of technology does not solve the key design and loses the stream characteristics.

dea-avc-003.text: A Firehose delivers to S3 with buffer 1 MB/60s, generating tens of thousands of tiny files per day and degrading the Athena. Consumption tolerates delay of up to 10 minutes. Which setting directly improves the layout of the files?
options: Decrease buffer to 1 second
Enable Bucket Version
Increase Firehose buffer (ex.: 128 MB/up 900 s), producing larger and fewer files
Change destination to DynamoDB
dea-avc-003.explanation: A) Incorrect: aggravates the problem of small files. B) Incorrect: versioning does not change the size of the files. C) Correct: larger buffers add more records per object — files in the hundreds of MB house are the target for efficient analytical reading; the extra delay fits in with SLA of 10 min. D) Incorrect: DynamoDB is not an analytical destination of the case.

dea-avc-004.text: A Spark job from AWS Glue failure with OutOfMemory errors when processing a dataset with transformations that embaralate (shuffle) many data. What setting of THEIR Glue attacks the problem without rewriting the job?
options: Convert job to Python shell
Disable Job Bookmarks
Switch the worker type to one with greater memory (e.g.: G).1X → G.2X) and adjust the number of workers
Reduce the number of workers to save
dea-avc-004.explanation: A) Incorrect: Python shell is single-node for light scripts, not Spark distributed. B) Incorrect: bookmarks control incrementality, not memory. C) Correct: the workers types of Glue define memory/CPU per executor — G.2X folds G's memory.1X; more memory by worker and appropriate parallelism solve OOM D) Incorrect: fewer workers concentrate more data per executor — worse OOM.

dea-avc-005.text: A date lake in Parquet in S3 now needs UPDATEs and DELETES at line level (corrections and LGPD), transactions ACID and time travel, keeping consultations via Athena and Spark. What modern approach attends?
options: Migrate all or lake to RDS
Use only versioning of S3 as 'transaction''
Manually rewrite the affected Parquet files to each fix
Adopt an open table format like Apache Iceberg on the S3, which supports ACID, upserts/deletes and time travel in integrated engines
dea-avc-005.explanation: A) Incorrect: move the entire lake to OLTP reverses the architecture. B) Incorrect: versioning of objects does not give semantics of transaction at line level. C) Incorrect: rewritten manual of Parquet is fragile, expensive and without atomicity. D) Correct: table formats like Iceberg add transactional layer to the lake: MERGE/DELETE, snapshots, time travel and schema evolution — supported by Athena, Glue, EMR/Spark.

dea-avc-006.text: A cluster EMR process night lots with flexible time. The team wants to drastically cut the cost of computing accepting occasional interruptions, SEM risk the data from HDFS nor the stability of the cluster. DUAS Do practices implement this? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Disable replication of the HDFS
Transient clusters with data on S3 (EMRFS), closed at the end of work
Spot in TODOS the nodes, including the primary
Permanent cluster with double core knots
Courts Spot in the knot TASK (not stored HDFS), keeping primary and core in On-Demand
dea-avc-006.explanation: (a) Incorrect: reduce replication of HDFS exchange cost for loss risk. EMRFS, the cluster becomes disposable — only the job window is paid. C) Incorrect: losing the primary drops the cluster; core in Spot risks blocks of HDFS. D) Incorrect: doubling core increases cost. Spot is recovered, the YARN Reexecutes the tasks; primary/core protected guarantee HDFS and coordination.

dea-avc-007.text: Continuous replication (CDC) of the DMS for the S3 is critical, and the business requires rapid detection when the latency of the replication goes beyond 5 minutes. How to monitor correctly?
options: Alarms of the CloudWatch on latency metrics of the task of DMS (CDCLatencySource/CDCLatencyTarget)
Manually check the count of lines once a day
Read the destination Bucket logs
Enable Trusted Advisor
dea-avc-007.explanation: (a) Correct: or DMS publish latency metrics of origin and destination per task — alarms > 300Incorrect: daily check discovers the delay hours later.: Trusted Advisor makes general recommendations, does not monitor tasks of DMS.

dea-avc-008.text: When deciding between Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Amazon MSK for a new streaming platform, which DOIS criteria correctly point to the MSK? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Latency must be less than 1 ms
Need for compatibility with the Kafka ecosystem (Kafka Connect, existing customers and tools)
Coverage exclusively for use without infrastructure provided
Fine broker/topic configuration requirements (topic retention, partitioning and Kafka parameters)
Desire for minimal management and more direct serverless integration with Firehose/Lambda
dea-avc-008.explanation: A) Incorrect: neither guarantee sub-millisecond. B) Correct: who already has code, connectors and operation Kafka migrates to MSK (c) Incorrect: MSK stock brokers (even Serverless has its own model); 'only by use' better describes Kinesis D) Correct: or MSK exposes the real Kafka — fine control of topics and broker parameters. E) Incorrect: this criterion points to the KINESIS (more managed/serverless and native integrations).

dea-avc-009.text: A lake receives micro-archives continuously in the raw layer. The team wants to keep the layer CURADA with Parquet files from ~256 MB, partitioned, without stopping the intake. What architecture standard solves?
options: Enable Transfer Acceleration
Periodical job of COMPACTION (Glue/Spark or OPTIMIZE in Iceberg tables) rewriting the micro-archives of the window in large files in the cured layer
Block intake until large files accumulate
Increase storage class for Glacier
dea-avc-009.explanation: A) Incorrect: upload acceleration does not rearrange files. B) Correct: the raw→curated pattern with scheduled compaction preserves continuous intake and efficient reading delivery; in Iceberg, the OPTIMIZE/rewrite does this in a managed way. C) Incorrect: stopping the intake creates delay and coupling. D) Incorrect: Glacier is archiving — worsening the query.

dea-avc-010.text: In a Spark job at EMR, o JOIN between a table fact of 2 TB and a dimension of 40 MB is causing massive shuffle. What classic technique eliminates shuffle from this JOIN?
options: Change the shape of the suit to CSV
Increase the number of partitions of the fact
Broadcast join: send the small size to all the executors, making the local joint (the Spark automatically does below the threshold, or via explicit hint/broadcast)
Breaking the size into a thousand partitions
dea-avc-010.explanation: A) Incorrect: CSV B) Incorrect: more partitions do not prevent the redistribution of the common joint. C) Correct: with the dimension in broadcast, each executor makes the joint locally against his slice of the fact — zero shuffle of the large table. D) Incorrect: slice 40 MB in a thousand partitions only creates overhead.

dea-avc-011.text: A function Lambda consume one Kinesis Stream via event source mapping. A 'poisonous' record makes the batch fail and shard processing TRAVA in infinite retreats, delaying everything. What configurations of the event source mapping unlocked the pipeline safely.?
options: Reduce the parallelism to 1
Increase function timeout
Delete and recreate the stream
Configure maximumRetryAttempts, bisectBatchOnFunctionError (divide batch to isolate bad record) and a fault destination (on-failure) for discarded records
dea-avc-011.explanation: A) Incorrect: less parallelism only leaves the delay worse. B) Incorrect: more timeout does not solve a record that always fails. C) Incorrect: recreate the stream loses data and does not prevent recurrence. D) Correct: limit retries + bisect isolates the poisonous record, and the fate of failure (SQS/SNS) preserves discarded for analysis — the shard returns to flow.

dea-avc-012.text: A table of the Athena has partitions per year/month/day and the metastore accumulated hundreds of thousands of partitions — the planning of the consultations was slow and the MSCK REPAIR which resource eliminates the dependency of registering each partition in the catalog?
options: Roll more crawlers in parallel
Increase partition limit
Partition Projection: o Athena CALCULA partitions from configured rules (intervals/formats), without consulting them in the metastore
Remove partitioning
dea-avc-012.explanation: A) Incorrect: crawlers continue to feed a giant metastore. B) Incorrect: the gargal is the enumeration, not the limit. C) Correct: with projection, the partitions have seen configuration function (e.g.: dates of 2020-01-01 until NOW) — instantaneous planning and end of MSCK/crawler for new partitions. D) Incorrect: without partitions, each query scans everything.
